decisions.reason: As a classic rye bread that fits the bakery’s core recipes, production skills, and everyday customer demand, it is easy for the firm to learn from and improve rather than withdraw quickly.
As a stated flagship product with a gold medal and a very strong fit to the firm’s confectionery and seasonal expertise, management would almost certainly continue backing it.
This seeded rye mixed bread is a close extension of existing bread know-how and ingredients, so the firm has high absorptive capacity to refine it and keep it in the assortment.
Although somewhat more niche in taste, the dark barley malt rye bread still builds directly on the bakery’s bread-making competence, making retention more likely than exit.
Marzipan stollen matches the firm’s seasonal pastry capabilities and allows learning within an already familiar product family, so it is likely to remain alongside the stronger raisin variant.

Ancient grain bread is slightly more experimental and may face narrower demand or higher ingredient costs, but it remains close enough to the firm’s artisanal bread expertise to justify keeping it for further learning.
